subject.title: [security] Lossy org normalization can grant access to org-shared leases across distinct org identifiers

question: What permanent org identity representation should Crabbox use for coordinator authorization when configured org strings contain characters that the current sanitizer rewrites?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the safe fix affects stored lease/run attribution and existing deployment config, so automation should not choose the migration and compatibility policy on its own.

options.title: Preserve exact or opaque org identity
options.body: Use exact raw org IDs or a collision-resistant opaque key for authorization/storage, keep a separate display-safe label, and add migration or compatibility handling for existing sanitized records.

options.title: Reject lossy org values
options.body: Fail configuration or authenticated requests whose org IDs would be rewritten, document the supported character set, and keep stored authorization keys unchanged for valid values.

options.title: Accept sanitized orgs as canonical
options.body: Document that rewritten org strings define the security boundary and close this as expected behavior after maintainer sign-off.

recommendation.title: Preserve exact or opaque org identity
recommendation.body: Use exact raw org IDs or a collision-resistant opaque key for authorization/storage, keep a separate display-safe label, and add migration or compatibility handling for existing sanitized records.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the affected org resolver and lease-sharing/run-history surfaces and have recent security-boundary history in this Worker area.
